painTitle: A good product doesn't reach brands on its own

pain.heading: App store installs aren't a sales motion
pain.body: Listings, reviews and partner directories bring in small stores on free plans. The established brands you want to land, the ones with real order volume, rarely browse an app store to find you.

pain.heading: The buyer changes with every product
pain.body: A logistics tool sells to an operations head, a retention platform to a CRM lead, an analytics product to a growth or revenue leader. One generic list of 'D2C founders' misses most of the people who sign.

pain.heading: Technical features, non-technical buyers
pain.body: Attribution models, API depth and integrations matter to you. A founder deciding between tools wants to know what happens to repeat purchase, delivery times or customer acquisition cost.

process.title: Merchant & ICP Mapping
process.body: We map the brands you serve best by platform, category, size and growth stage, and the role that owns the problem, before any outreach starts.

process.title: Verified Buyer Lists
process.body: Hand-verified founders, operations, CRM and growth leaders at those brands, segmented so each group gets its own message. No scraped app store lists.

process.title: Use-Case Outreach
process.body: Messaging built around the operational problem each segment feels, translated from your product's technical strengths into business outcomes.

process.title: Qualified Demo Handoff
process.body: Interested merchants land in your calendar with their platform, volume and use case noted. Your product and sales team runs the demo.

caseCards.headline: A cold email engine that filled the demo calendar in six weeks

caseCards.body: A Shopify app company had a useful product but struggled to reach brands with the right requirements. We picked merchants by size, category and growth stage, and led outreach with use cases instead of a generic demo offer.
